title: けど — but, though
explanation: けど joins two things that pull against each other: {高|たか}いけど、おいしい — it’s expensive, but good. It also softens: ending with けど leaves the sentence open, which makes a request or a "no" gentler: ちょっと{聞|き}きたいんですけど… (I’d like to ask something…), {行|い}きたいけど… (I’d like to go, but…).
natural: The everyday "but" in conversation, casual or polite (ですけど). With your partner and friends it’s the default.
stiff: けど is spoken language. In writing and formal speech use が (next lesson); けれども is the fuller, more careful version.

examples.japanese: この店は高いけど、すごくおいしい。
examples.furigana: この{店|みせ}は{高|たか}いけど、すごくおいしい。
examples.english: This place is expensive, but it’s really good.

gap.before: この{店|みせ}は{高|たか}い

combine.a: この{店|みせ}は{高|たか}い。

examples.japanese: 日本語は難しいけど、楽しいです。
examples.furigana: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しいけど、{楽|たの}しいです。
examples.english: Japanese is hard, but it’s fun.

gap.before: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しい

combine.a: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しいです。

examples.japanese: 行きたいけど、今日はちょっと…
examples.furigana: {行|い}きたいけど、{今日|きょう}はちょっと…
examples.english: I’d love to go, but today’s a bit…

gap.why: けど softens a "no" — you don’t even have to finish the sentence.

examples.japanese: すみません、ちょっと聞きたいんですけど…
examples.furigana: すみません、ちょっと{聞|き}きたいんですけど…
examples.english: Excuse me, I have a quick question…

gap.before: すみません、ちょっと{聞|き}きたいんです
gap.note: が works too — a little more formal.
